title: Ginject Concurrency Model
purpose: Document thread safety guarantees and race conditions

http_request_model.synchronization: implicit (each request gets own context object from pool)

websocket_connection_model.synchronization: channelized (readLoop → handler → memorybroker.Publish → writeLoop via channel)

event.Event.description: Event listeners and emitters (Node-style EventEmitter, no topic pattern matching)
event.Event.synchronization: single sync.RWMutex over two maps (opts, onceOpts); Emit copies listeners to a private slice before unlocking, then invokes outside the lock

memorybroker.Broker.synchronization: single sync.RWMutex over 4 maps, no sharding; PublishAsync additionally coordinates via sync.WaitGroup so Close() can drain in-flight async goroutines before clearing state

not_thread_safe.handler_closures: if handler captures mutable state, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.controller_state: if controller has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.provider_state: if provider has mutable fields, not thread-safe
not_thread_safe.module_state_during_init: module is mutable during app.Create(), must not call Create() concurrently

concurrency_guarantees.http_request: each request is fully isolated, no race conditions possible
concurrency_guarantees.ws_connection: each connection is single-threaded, no race conditions within connection
concurrency_guarantees.message_broker: concurrent-safe pub/sub via a single RWMutex; not lock-free (RWMutex-guarded, not literally atomic ops)

scenario_1.name: Retaining context after request
scenario_1.description: Handler stores context reference, reused in next request
scenario_1.prevention: never hold onto context after handler returns

scenario_2.name: Mutable provider state
scenario_2.description: Provider with mutable fields shared across requests
scenario_2.example: type Service struct { counter int }; counter++ in handler
scenario_2.prevention: use sync.Mutex if mutable state needed, or make stateless

scenario_3.name: Raw websocket access
scenario_3.description: Handler writes directly to conn, fanout also writes
scenario_3.impact: concurrent writes to connection, message corruption
scenario_3.example: conn.Send() in handler while fanout sends
scenario_3.prevention: use Publisher only, never raw conn access

scenario_4.name: Module mutation during Create
scenario_4.example: Create() called from two goroutines simultaneously
scenario_4.prevention: Create() must be called exactly once, before any requests

memory_safety.message_broker: lightweight pub/sub (no message buffering except WS send channels)

deadlock_risks.risk_2: memorybroker.Broker.Close() called synchronously from within a handler that was itself dispatched by PublishAsync — self-deadlock, VERIFIED (see anti-patterns-gotchas.md). Close()'s wg.Wait() can never return because wg.Done() for that goroutine only runs after the handler (which is blocked in Close()) returns. NOT a bug in the locking, an inherent property of waiting on your own in-flight WaitGroup entry; documented as unsupported rather than special-cased
deadlock_risks.risk_2_note: Reentrancy is otherwise SAFE and verified by test: a handler calling Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Publish/PublishAsync (including on itself) does not deadlock, because publishInternal releases its RLock before invoking any handler — Close() called from a SYNC Publish handler is also safe (Publish isn't WaitGroup-tracked)
deadlock_risks.prevention: keep pipeline stages lock-free and non-blocking; never call Close() synchronously from a PublishAsync-dispatched handler

cancellation_handling.graceful_shutdown: no built-in support, must implement application-level
